findings.requirement: BIZQ-01 §4.3 requires plausible alternatives with comparable specificity and guards against a systematic answer-form cue.
findings.rationale: Fourteen keyed choices are strictly longer than every distractor. The repeated pattern is qualitative: the key is a complete multi-clause prescription naming the related fields, publication boundary, and reader outcome; wrong choices usually state one partial write, caller-side repair, or broad lock. Examples i007 is 138 characters versus an 84-character longest distractor; i018 is 140 versus 93. In context, the answer can be selected by its completeness/atomicity wording instead of deriving the exact related state boundary.
findings.correction: Keep the case facts and correct decision. Rework choice sets so plausible alternatives represent complete, case-specific competing boundaries and require comparing the stated invariant. Do not pad or target a length/count.

findings.requirement: BIZQ-01 §4.1–4.2 requires one defensible answer grounded in visible facts; the unit objective is the smallest coherent state change, separate from unrelated workloads.
findings.rationale: The repeated global-lock distractor is diagnosed as wrong because it blocks unrelated work, but several prompts do not state that unrelated operations must continue. In those cases a coarse lock can satisfy the stated atomicity/visibility condition if all participants honor it; its inefficiency alone does not make it incorrect. For example, i003 says one episode is being remapped but does not require other episodes to proceed, and i004 does not say permission checks for unrelated users must remain available. The wrong-option message supplies an unstated performance/availability fact.
findings.correction: For affected stems, make the required independent work/availability boundary visible when it is part of the objective, or replace the global-lock distractor with a plausible alternative that demonstrably violates the stated invariant. Keep this tied to the existing smallest-boundary objective; do not introduce a new performance requirement.
